chunks: "If you forget to wipe your head, then wipe it and your feet with the remaining moisture from your wudu (ablution). If there is nothing left in your hand of the moisture of your wudu (ablution), then take from what remains of it in your beard and wipe your head and your feet with it. If you do not have a beard, then take from your eyebrows and the lashes of your eyes and wipe your head and your feet with it. And if nothing remains of the moisture of your wudu (ablution), you repeat the wudu (ablution)."

key_terms.أَعَدْتَ: you repeat, meaning the wudu (ablution) must be redone
key_terms.حَاجِبَيْكَ: your eyebrows, as an alternative source of moisture
key_terms.رَأْسِكَ: your head, the place to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.رِجْلَيْكَ: your feet, also to be wiped here
key_terms.لِحْيَتِكَ: your beard, from which remaining moisture may be taken
key_terms.مَسْحَ: wiping as a required act in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they forget to wipe the head during wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who forgets the wiping of the head in wudu (ablution). It explains that the wiping should be completed using the remaining moisture of the original wudu (ablution), and if no such moisture remains at all, then the wudu (ablution) must be repeated.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.134 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"If you forget to wipe your head, then wipe it and your feet with the remaining moisture from your wudu. If there is no moisture left in your hands from the wudu, then take what remains in your beard and wipe your head and feet with it. If you do not have a beard, then take from your eyebrows and the lashes of your eyes and wipe your head and feet with that. If there is no moisture left from your wudu, then repeat the wudu."
